about: How the interviewers' voices say words they get wrong (EC-11.11). An entry is here only because the voice said the term and Whisper did not hear it back, and its respelling WAS heard back (research/lexicon/probe.py). `exact`: only that casing (an acronym). Names (2026-10-11): an Indian name read with English letter rules comes back right from Whisper and still sounds foreign, so the read-back test cannot judge them; they are respelled by ear. Names (2026-10-11, second pass): 151 common Indian names were said by an Indian voice and read back; where a respelling came back better than the plain name it replaced it. Names not listed go through lexicon.respell_names.
